title: Act on Restoration of Honor to Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the promotion of human rights and national unity by restoring the honor of persons and the Buddhist community that suffered harm in connection with the October 27 Buddhist Persecution. <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>
1. The term "October 27 Buddhist Persecution" means the incident in October 1980 in which the Joint Investigation Unit of the Joint Investigation Headquarters of the Martial Law Command forcibly took into custody and investigated monks of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism and other persons associated with Buddhism under the pretext of purifying the Buddhist community, and the military and police jointly searched Buddhist temples, hermitages, and other such places throughout the country under the pretext of arresting persons wanted for violating martial law proclamations and subversive elements;
2. The term "victim" means a person who died or suffered injury or disability as a result of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution;
3. The term "affected religious organization" means the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, whose religious dignity and honor were impaired by the October 27 Buddhist Persecution, and a Buddhist temple to which a victim belonged at the time of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution.

Article 3 (Restoration of Honor to Victims and Affected Religious Organizations)
(1) A Committee for Deliberation on the Restoration of Honor to Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established under the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism to deliberate and decide on matters concerning the restoration of honor to victims or affected religious organizations (hereinafter referred to as "victims, etc."). <Amended on Feb. 3, 2016>
(2) The Committee shall deliberate and decide on the following matters: <Amended on May 22, 2013; Feb. 3, 2016>
1. Deleted. <Feb. 3, 2016>
2. Matters concerning the restoration of honor to victims, etc.;
3. Matters concerning the payment of medical assistance to victims;
4. Matters concerning the construction of a memorial hall for the October 27 Buddhist Persecution;
5. Other matters concerning assistance prescribed by Presidential Decree in connection with the restoration of honor to victims, etc.
(3) The Committee shall consist of no more than 11 members, including one chairperson.
(4) Members shall be commissioned or appointed by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience and relevant public officials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the chairperson shall be elected by and from among the members. <Amended on Feb. 3, 2016; Aug. 8, 2023>
(5) Other matters necessary for the organization and operation of the Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 3-2 (Deemed Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)
Members of the Committee who are not public officials shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Articles 127 and 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 4 Deleted. <Feb. 3, 2016>

Article 5 (Medical Assistance)
(1) Among persons who suffered injury or disability as a result of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution, those who, at the time this Act enters into force, require continued treatment, constant nursing care, or the use of assistive devices due to such injury or disability shall be paid, in a lump sum, the expenses for treatment, nursing care, and the purchase of assistive devices; provided, persons who were taken into custody at the time of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution and sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment for another unlawful act shall be excluded. <Amended on May 18, 2021; Aug. 8, 2023>
(2) When medical assistance is paid under paragraph (1), interim interest shall be deducted using the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate.
(3) The right to receive medical assistance shall not be transferred, provided as security, or attached.
(4) Matters necessary concerning eligibility for medical assistance, the criteria for payment, and other matters under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Recovery of Medical Assistance)
(1) The State shall recover medical assistance received by a person in any of the following cases: <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>
1. Where the person received medical assistance by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the medical assistance was paid in error.
(2) Where a person required to repay medical assistance under paragraph (1) fails to repay the relevant amount, the amount shall be collected in the same manner as delinquent national taxes. <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>

Article 7 (Fact-Finding Investigations)
(1) To deliberate and decide on the matters specified in Article 3 (2), the Committee may hear testimony or statements from victims, witnesses, or other persons with relevant information, or, where it deems necessary, conduct an inspection of evidence or an investigation, or request necessary cooperation from the heads of relevant agencies; in such cases, the heads of the relevant agencies shall comply without delay unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>
(2) Any person may submit materials to the Committee or freely give testimony in connection with the restoration of honor to victims, etc. and the payment and recovery of medical assistance, and shall not suffer any disadvantage as a result.

ADDENDA <Act No. 8995, Mar. 28, 2008>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

(2) Deleted. <Feb. 3, 2016>

ADDENDA <Act No. 9947, Jan. 25, 2010>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 11776, May 22, 2013>

This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation; provided, the amended provisions of Article 4 (1) and paragraph (2) of the Addenda to the Act on Restoration of Honor to Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution (Act No. 8995) shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 13954, Feb. 3, 2016>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on June 30, 2016.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures concerning Affairs under Jurisdiction)
The affairs under the jurisdiction of the former Committee for Deliberation on the Restoration of Honor to Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution under the Prime Minister at the time this Act enters into force shall be succeeded to by the Committee for Deliberation on the Restoration of Honor to Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution under the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism established pursuant to the amended provisions of Article 3.

ADDENDA <Act No. 16044, Dec. 24, 2018>

This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 18146, May 18, 2021>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Act Partially Amending 43 Acts under the Jurisdiction of the Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee to Improve Legal Terminology) <Act No. 19592, Aug. 8, 2023>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
